newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Polaris II fund raises $32 million.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Polaris II fund raises $32 million.

text.p: Israel's Polaris II venture capital fund said on Tuesday that it had raised an additional $32 million from U.S. investors.
The fund had already raised $50 million from Israeli and foreign investors and expects to raise another $30 million.

Polaris said it hoped the final $30 million would come from foreign pension funds, but said this was contingent on the Israeli government amending tax regulations to exempt them from capital gains tax.

Polaris II was formed by Dovrat Shrem Group, an Israeli investment house, together with the U.S. investment bank Cowen & Co. and the Travelers Group. Other investors include BEA, a U.S. fund-management company, and Claridge Israel, an investment company controlled by Charles Bronfman.
The fund is investing primarily in high technology companies specialising in telecommunications, software, medical and other electronics, and biotechnology.
